subject: Microbiology & immunology
summary: Taenia solium is a pork tapeworm that can cause cysticercosis when larvae lodge in tissues, especially the brain. Clinical thinking focuses on exposure, symptom patterns, and imaging rather than memorising parasite features.

sections.p: Taenia solium is a flat, segmented cestode that lives in the human intestine as the adult, but its larvae can invade extra‑intestinal sites, producing cysticercosis.
b: Adult tapeworm in gut; larvae in tissues

sections.p: The adult worm has a scolex with four suckers and a rostellum, a long strobila of proglottids, and releases gravid segments that are passed in stool.
Humans are definitive hosts; pigs are intermediate. Humans acquire infection by eating undercooked pork or via fecal‑oral contamination. Larvae encyst in tissues after ingestion of eggs.
Cysticercosis is the main disease, presenting as neurocysticercosis, ocular, or muscular forms. Neurocysticercosis is the leading cause of acquired epilepsy in endemic areas.
Diagnosis integrates exposure history, imaging, and serology. Neurocysticercosis is staged by cyst number, location, and inflammatory response.
b: History of pork, travel, or pig exposure

sections.p: Treat the parasite with antiparasitic drugs, but avoid monotherapy in neurocysticercosis to prevent severe inflammation. Adjunctive steroids reduce edema. Control focuses on sanitation and pig husbandry.
Remember that neurocysticercosis can mimic other causes of seizures. Imaging is key; serology is supportive. Steroids are essential when starting antiparasitics.
b: Use steroids with antiparasitics in neurocysticercosis

sections.p: Echinococcosis (hydatid disease) and neurocysticercosis can both present with cystic brain lesions, but hydatid cysts are larger and have daughter cysts.
Serology may be negative in single or calcified cysts; imaging may miss small cysts; stool microscopy may miss intermittent shedding.
Treat the underlying infection, provide seizure control, monitor for raised intracranial pressure, and counsel on food hygiene.
Urgent care is needed for seizures, signs of increased intracranial pressure, or ocular involvement.

t.a: What is the most common symptom of neurocysticercosis?
t.b: Seizures, especially in children and young adults.
Yes, by cooking pork thoroughly, practicing hand hygiene, and improving sanitation.

t.a: Why are steroids used with antiparasitics?
t.b: They reduce inflammation from dying larvae, preventing worsening seizures or edema.

whenToSeekHelp: Seizures, vomiting, papilledema, sudden visual loss

exam: Describe the life cycle of Taenia solium and explain how it leads to neurocysticercosis.
Explain why steroids are added to antiparasitic therapy in neurocysticercosis and what complications may arise if omitted.
Outline the diagnostic workup for a patient with suspected neurocysticercosis presenting with new-onset seizures.
